spec: Which selector field addresses a graph when a WHOLE GRAPH IMAGE is moved — a sync push, a sync pull, or a bench corpus transfer. Three modules compose this selector and none of them can import the others (the only shared contract is generated protobuf), so the rule is written here once and read by a test in EACH module: cmd/knowledge (the sync arms, through tools.syncGraphSelector), cmd/server-bench (the corpus transfer, through bench.graphRef.selector()). A drift on either side reds on that side rather than showing up as a transfer that quietly moved the wrong graph. PRACTICE IS THE ROW THAT MOVED TWICE AND THE REASON THIS FILE EXISTS. The family is a singleton for node reads and writes, so an unselected address is the combined graph named 'default' and carries no instance field at all. For one release the eight pre-singleton graph IMAGES still existed on both sides, so an image move naming one of them addressed it through `language`, the legacy selector the server's practice policy row consumed — and deleting practice's case from a switch was not a fix, because it dropped practice into the default arm, which sent exactly the `name` the policy refused. Those images are gone from the plane and the policy row consumes nothing, so EVERY practice image move carries no instance field: the two practice rows below are the whole practice rule, and any other name is REFUSED rather than composed into a selector. CHECKS IS THE SECOND FAMILY THAT CARRIES NOTHING, for the same reason practice's combined graph does: it holds one graph and its per-language grouping is a metadata key inside it. NO FAMILY IS ACCOUNT-KEYED AND THE FIELD IS GONE FROM THE VOCABULARY: the account-keyed inventory families retired with their built-in collectors, and a collected inventory graph is a registered custom type now, which keys by name like every other registered type. The wire field survives on GraphSelector because removing a proto field is its own change; no image move composes one. `language` survives on the wire on the same terms and for the same reason, and no image move composes one either — which is why it is absent from the vocabulary below. THE ROWS THAT AGREE ARE HERE ON PURPOSE — linkage, web, pdf and a registered custom type all key by name on every side, and a confirmatory row costs nothing while its absence would leave a reader guessing whether the family was considered. WHAT THIS TABLE CANNOT CARRY: a REFUSED spelling. A practice name the family cannot address has no (field, value) answer at all, because the arm refuses before composing a selector; that half of the rule is pinned by the refusal tests beside each module's sync arm, not here.

field_vocabulary.name: GraphSelector.name
field_vocabulary.none: no instance field at all: the family holds one graph and its resolver consumes nothing
